channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE B
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

Discover Korean travel expressions in an engaging and entertaining way with skits performed by ONF?s Hyo-jin, Seung-jun, Wyatt, and Alexa. channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: K-FOOD CLASS
channel.desc: Chef Joseph Lidgerwood?s class is? A Little Too Special! A K-FOOD experience crafted like no other ? Now Open! As global interest in Korean culture continues to thrive, K-FOOD has become one of its most compelling pillars. And today, people aren?t just curious about how it tastes. They want to learn how it?s made. Joseph Lidgerwood, chef-owner of the Michelin two-star restaurant EVETT, is an Australian chef who has developed a deep connection to Korea?s traditional jang and its ingredients. Now, he?s ready to share what he calls the ?the true taste of Korea.? Each episode welcomes a new group of participants from around the world, learning the all-time favorites such as Korean fried chicken, jaeyuk bokkeum, ganjang gejang, godeungeo kimchijjim, and bajirak sujebi, all reimagined through Joseph?s unique style. The atmosphere in the kitchen, shaped by curiosity, focus, and genuine interaction between Joseph and his students, often becomes as memorable as the food they create. You?ll take home the recipes, of course. But what truly sets this class apart is the moments shared along the way, the laughter, the discoveries, and the way flavor bridges cultures. Experience the depth, joy, and creativity of K-FOOD in Joseph?s A Little Too Special: K-FOOD Class!

channel.title: K-CHAT: CONVERSING IN KOREAN
channel.desc: \"What would you say in Korean in a situation like this?\" Discover how to express yourself in various daily life situations in Korean, from greetings and making friends to making promises and ordering your favorite food. A comprehensive Korean program designed to teach Korean language through real-life situations! A global initiative featuring top performers. Benefit from clear and friendly explanations by Peter Vint, a British TV personality who mastered Korean himself. Engage in lively Korean language lessons taught by Korean-American idols Aaron and Alexa! Experience a delightful Korean language course that delves into culture, trends, and even generational nuances. Each lesson is a concise 10-minute package, including scenarios, explanations, and practical exercises. Enjoy short, yet entertaining content that will also provide insight into culture, trends, and generational diversity. With just a glance, you'll be able to speak Korean fluently. Embark on an enjoyable and refreshing journey through our Korean language course.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: K-CHAT: TRAVEL IN KOREA
channel.desc: Simple and Fun Korean Lessons, ?K-Chat: Travel in Korea? What are the most useful expressions visitors to Korea can use right away?From arriving at the airport to finding your hotel and exploring popular travel destinations, this program offers practical expressions for your Korean language journey. It also covers traditional Korean culture and essential travel information, making it an invaluable resource for beginner to intermediate learners! Discover Korean travel expressions in an engaging and entertaining way with skits performed by ONF?s Hyo-jin, Seung-jun, Wyatt, and Alexa. With clear and accessible explanations from Hye-rim of the Wonder Girls, a graduate of Hankuk University of Foreign Studies, you?ll systematically improve your Korean!

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: K-FOOD CLASS
channel.desc: Chef Joseph Lidgerwood?s class is? A Little Too Special! A K-FOOD experience crafted like no other ? Now Open! As global interest in Korean culture continues to thrive, K-FOOD has become one of its most compelling pillars. And today, people aren?t just curious about how it tastes. They want to learn how it?s made. Joseph Lidgerwood, chef-owner of the Michelin two-star restaurant EVETT, is an Australian chef who has developed a deep connection to Korea?s traditional jang and its ingredients. Now, he?s ready to share what he calls the ?the true taste of Korea.? Each episode welcomes a new group of participants from around the world, learning the all-time favorites such as Korean fried chicken, jaeyuk bokkeum, ganjang gejang, godeungeo kimchijjim, and bajirak sujebi, all reimagined through Joseph?s unique style. The atmosphere in the kitchen, shaped by curiosity, focus, and genuine interaction between Joseph and his students, often becomes as memorable as the food they create. You?ll take home the recipes, of course. But what truly sets this class apart is the moments shared along the way, the laughter, the discoveries, and the way flavor bridges cultures. Experience the depth, joy, and creativity of K-FOOD in Joseph?s A Little Too Special: K-FOOD Class!

What are the most useful expressions visitors to Korea can use right away?From arriving at the airport to finding your hotel and exploring popular travel destinations, this program offers practical expressions for your Korean language journey. It also covers traditional Korean culture and essential travel information, making it an invaluable resource for beginner to intermediate learners! Discover Korean travel expressions in an engaging and entertaining way with skits performed by ONF?s Hyo-jin, Seung-jun, Wyatt, and Alexa. With clear and accessible explanations from Hye-rim of the Wonder Girls, a graduate of Hankuk University of Foreign Studies, you?ll systematically improve your Korean!

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE B
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: K-FOOD CLASS
channel.desc: Chef Joseph Lidgerwood?s class is? A Little Too Special! A K-FOOD experience crafted like no other ? Now Open! As global interest in Korean culture continues to thrive, K-FOOD has become one of its most compelling pillars. And today, people aren?t just curious about how it tastes. They want to learn how it?s made. Joseph Lidgerwood, chef-owner of the Michelin two-star restaurant EVETT, is an Australian chef who has developed a deep connection to Korea?s traditional jang and its ingredients. Now, he?s ready to share what he calls the ?the true taste of Korea.? Each episode welcomes a new group of participants from around the world, learning the all-time favorites such as Korean fried chicken, jaeyuk bokkeum, ganjang gejang, godeungeo kimchijjim, and bajirak sujebi, all reimagined through Joseph?s unique style. The atmosphere in the kitchen, shaped by curiosity, focus, and genuine interaction between Joseph and his students, often becomes as memorable as the food they create. You?ll take home the recipes, of course. But what truly sets this class apart is the moments shared along the way, the laughter, the discoveries, and the way flavor bridges cultures. Experience the depth, joy, and creativity of K-FOOD in Joseph?s A Little Too Special: K-FOOD Class!

In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

Through [Decoded: The AI Conversations], we will examine where this technology is heading and how it is changing our lives and society, together with leaders guiding the Korean AI industry. This journey features Dr. Kang Sung-ju, also known as the science communicator \"Hang sung\", as a fixed panelist. In the conversation among the MC, the panelist, and the guests, complex AI concepts are naturally \"decoded\" into everyday language. This will be a platform that vividly delivers the frontline of AI innovation where technology, industry, and policy intersect.

channel.title: DIPLOMAT'S ARCHIVE: HIDDEN STORIES
channel.desc: As of April 2025, S. Korea has established diplomatic relations with a total of 194 countries. Among them are countries that have had ties and exchanges with Korea for hundreds of years. With such long-standing relationships with so many nations, might there be fascinating hidden stories between Korea and the rest of the world that we don?t know yet? \"Diplomat?s Archives: Hidden Stories\" begins with this very question. Together with foreign embassies in Korea, the series uncovers and sheds light on meaningful yet lesser-known stories between Korea and other countries. Through this, we aim to reaffirm the deep friendships that have been built over time, highlight how countries are interconnected?bilaterally and multilaterally? and emphasize the importance of cooperation on the global stage today.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Matsuri: The Heartbeat Of Japan
channel.desc: Gojinjo Taiko is a wild, powerful performance by masked drummers. It originated 400 years ago in the small coastal community of Nafune-machi in Ishikawa Prefecture. The story goes that, faced with an imminent attack by a powerful warlord, villagers used improvised masks to disguise themselves as oni (demons), and scared away the approaching forces. Gojinjo Taiko is performed not only at the summer matsuri (festival) but at local hotels in everyday life, as a form of community revitalization.

channel.title: Nun's Cookbook
channel.desc: Seasonal recipes from the nuns of Otowasan Kannonji Temple: Furofuki daikon with two sauces. First, prepare the sauces using a white miso base, one with boiled butterbur and the other with yuzu peel and juice. Serve with boiled daikon for a crispy spring treat.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Journeys In Japan
channel.desc: British explorer and writer Isabella Bird arrived in Japan in 1878, just 10 years after start of the Meiji Era. \"Unbeaten Tracks in Japan\" is her highly praised account of her journey deep into Japan's hinterland.\nAfter traveling from Yokohama all the way up to Hokkaido, Bird then made her way to Kansai, where she visited Kyoto, Nara and Mie Prefectures. As a student, Rachael Aoki studied in Kyoto at a university that Isabella visited during her stay. In this episode, Rachael retraces Bird's steps from the Nara deer park to the Ise Jingu Shrine, with a stop at Hasedera Temple en route.

channel.desc: British explorer and writer Isabella Bird arrived in Japan in 1878, just 10 years after start of the Meiji Era. \"Unbeaten Tracks in Japan\" is her highly praised account of her journey deep into Japan's hinterland.\nAfter traveling from Yokohama all the way up to Hokkaido, Bird then made her way to Kansai, where she visited Kyoto, Nara and Mie Prefectures. As a student, Rachael Aoki studied in Kyoto at a university that Isabella visited during her stay. In this episode, Rachael retraces Bird's steps from the Nara deer park to the Ise Jingu Shrine, with a stop at Hasedera Temple en route.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: The Seasons Of Yamato
channel.desc: Hannyaji Temple is known as \"Kosumosudera (cosmos flower temple).\" During wintertime, the main flowers are daffodils. They bloom as if they are competing around the stone statues of Buddhists, which were dedicated in appreciation for curing diseases. Are those flowers praising the virtues of the Buddha or showing off their beauty? The 13-story stone pagoda, which has stood there since the Kamakura period, is towering against the crisp blue winter sky.\n\n*According to the 24 Solar Terms of Reiwa 4 (2022), Shoukan is from January 5 to 20.

channel.name: Thrill ID
channel.title: Red Snow
channel.desc: Keinginan Olivia untuk bertemu dengan vampir sungguhan terwujud saat Luke mendatangi kabinnya untuk mencari bantuan. Namun, keinginannya berubah menjadi mimpi buruk saat teman-teman vampir Luke melacak keberadaannya.

channel.name: Thrill ID
channel.title: The Ones You Didn't Burn
channel.desc: Setelah kematian sang ayah, Nathan dan saudarinya kembali ke kampung halaman untuk menjual rumah mereka. Di sana, Nathan mendapati bahwa rumah itu ternyata milik nenek moyang dua wanita yang diduga penyihir.

channel.name: Thrill ID
channel.title: Sinister
channel.desc: Jia Hao dan teman-temannya berkumpul untuk merayakan ulang tahun Jia Hao di sebuah vila. Namun, perayaan itu berubah menjadi peristiwa yang mengerikan saat mereka terhubung ke sebuah gim virtual realitas nan mematikan.

channel.name: Thrill ID
channel.title: Night Watch
channel.desc: Wang Ren Jie bekerja sebagai penjaga malam setelah hilang ingatan karena kecelakaan mobil. Saat jam menunjukkan tengah malam, ia pun bertugas di gedung terbengkalai dan menemukan tiga jiwa yang tersesat di sana.

channel.name: Thrill ID
channel.title: The Windmill Massacre

channel.name: Thrill ID
channel.title: No. 82 Haunted House
channel.desc: Demi menenangkan arwah putra sulung keluarga Mu yang tewas pada malam pernikahannya, seorang ART pun dinikahkan dan dikubur hidup-hidup. Sejak saat itu, rumah Mu dihantui oleh serangkaian kejadian yang mengerikan.

channel.name: Thrill ID
channel.title: Night At The Eagle Inn

channel.name: Thrill ID
